svg.text: Figure 19: Hot and high: density altitude
The same aircraft on two days. Thin air gives the propellers less to push on, and the aircraft flies as if it were much higher than it is.
the air is nearly as dense as at sea level
thin air: more throttle for the same hover
High density altitude reduces propeller efficiency and performance.
Less thrust and less lift: a weaker climb, more throttle to hover, a shorter flight, and a longer takeoff for a fixed wing.
Density altitude rises with elevation, temperature and humidity. Rule of thumb: about 120 ft per °C above the standard day
(15 °C at sea level, 2 °C cooler per 1,000 ft). Pilot’s Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge, chapter 11.
